title: How to Dress in Your 60s: 5 Modern Style Tips | The Stitch Fix Guide To Dressing In Your 60s
summary: Explore fashion for women over 60 with tips for creating modern outfits, mixing timeless pieces with trends and finding clothes that fit your style.
body_markdown:
In your 60s, great style is all about wearing what feels like you. Mix tried-and-true favorites with fresh trends, play with color or switch up your go-to silhouettes. These five tips will help you keep your wardrobe feeling current while staying true to your personal style. Love the idea, but want a Stylist to handle it for you?[Take your style quiz](https://www.stitchfix.com/signup) to get started.


## **1. Embrace Color and Prints**


Style doesn’t have an age limit! Add personality to your wardrobe with vibrant colors, playful patterns or a statement accessory that makes an outfit feel uniquely yours. Stylist Julie suggests pairing a brightly colored printed scarf with a sleek monochromatic ensemble for a chic look.


> “Wear a black cashmere sweater and black trousers, and add a red printed scarf to introduce a fun pop of color as the focal point of your outfit.” — **Stylist Julie**


## **2. Choose Comfort without Sacrificing Style**


Comfort and personal style can go hand in hand. Stylist Caro recommends you look for[breathable fabrics](https://www.stitchfix.com/women/blog/style-guide/guide-breathable-summer-fabrics/) , soft knits and relaxed silhouettes that feel good to wear while still helping you put together a polished outfit.


> “Try linen-blend trousers with a crisp cotton shirt and a softly structured blazer. It’s an easy combination that feels comfortable while still looking put together.” — **Stylist Caro**


## **3. Mix Classic Pieces with Modern Trends**


If you’re wondering how to dress at 60 and look modern, you don’t need to replace your entire wardrobe. Start with the classic pieces you already love, then bring in current silhouettes or styling details to keep your outfits feeling fresh.


> “Try wide-leg jeans with modern sneakers or a classic blazer over a graphic tee. I love the juxtaposition of adding a little edge to an everyday look. It makes the outfit feel fun and unexpected!” — **Stylist Julie**


## **4. Invest in Elevated Basics**


Build your wardrobe around versatile staples like great-fitting denim, tailored trousers, crisp button-downs and lightweight sweaters. These timeless pieces make everyday styling effortless. Stylist Jackie adds the finishing touches with loafers and a statement necklace for a polished, put-together look that feels effortlessly chic.


## **5. Prioritize Fit Over Size**


Well-fitting clothes instantly create a polished look. Focus on pieces that skim the body without feeling too tight or oversized and don’t be afraid of a little tailoring.


> “Try a half-tuck with your favorite blouse or sweater to define your waist and create a flattering silhouette. Pair it with straight-leg jeans or tailored trousers for an effortlessly polished look!” —Stylist Jackie


## **Essential Clothes for Women Over 60**


A versatile wardrobe starts with pieces you can wear in different ways and make your own. From accessories that add personality to dependable denim and statement outerwear, these essentials can help you build outfits around your personal style.


### **Eye-catching Accessories**


Accessories like scarves, bags and jewelry are your style’s secret weapon. They offer an easy way to switch up any look—just changing accessories can take a work look to weekend-fabulous. Accessories are also a fun way to experiment with colors and patterns you don’t typically wear.


> “Embrace updated bag shapes that feel both current and easy to wear, such as sleek east-west shoulder bags that tuck neatly under your arm, crescent crossbodies that keep things hands-free or leather bucket bags that keep your essentials organized.” —Stylist Julie


### **Jeans for Women Over 60**


When it comes to[jeans for women over 60](https://www.stitchfix.com/women/blog/style-guide/your-perfect-jeans/) , it’s time to break the rules. There are classic styles that go with everything (hello, straight-leg, dark-wash denim), but you can also mix it up with a different rise, wider leg or even a cropped or distressed hemline. Stylist Jackie recommends experimenting with trending silhouettes like wide-leg or cropped jeans.


> “Balance a relaxed fit with a more structured top, add a chic belt to define your waist and finish with a pointed-toe flat or ankle boot for an effortlessly polished look.” —Stylist Jackie


### **Statement Outerwear**


Whether you’re headed out for a night on the town,[a wedding](https://www.stitchfix.com/women/blog/trends-and-occasions/wedding-attires-women) or just around the corner, nothing says sophistication like an incredible coat. Over the years, you’ve purchased outerwear that does the job and keeps you warm.


For a coat that goes beyond function, look for a great fit and details that add personality to your outfit. Consider luxurious fabrics like brocade, cashmere or faux fur for winter or a raincoat in a standout color or a fabulous trench for chillier spring months. Stylist Caro recommends updating your winter wardrobe with a coat that has an interesting neckline.


> “Try a funnel-neck coat with straight-leg jeans, a fine-knit sweater and ankle boots for everyday wear, or a scarf coat over tailored trousers for a dressier look. Both styles make a statement without needing much else.” —Stylist Caro
